title: Register reset run
statement: Let $K_0,B,P$ be natural numbers, let $S$ be a machine state, and let $M\colon\mathbb{Z}\to\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$ be a memory configuration. If every register value of $S$ is at most $B$, then the machine has a finite guarded run from the first reset control state, initialized with $S$, memory $M$, and head position $0$, to the move control state. At the endpoint, the registers $U,V,w,K,B_s$ are zero, and every other register retains its value from $S$; the memory and head position are unchanged.
hypotheses_covered: Every register value of $S$ is at most $B$
